rows.label: Most items it asked for at once

intro: Companies now let AI agents work on their systems. An AI agent is a computer program that does tasks for a person or a team, often many tasks in a row without asking anyone.
This study is about one company's code server: the place where the company keeps its software. The server is what we want to protect. It cannot see what an agent is thinking, only what the agent did.

Each card shows one agent's day. For each line you see what is usual for that same agent (its own last 3 months, up to yesterday) and what it did today. Agents differ a lot, so compare each agent only with itself.
A range like "20-65" shows this agent's usual days. About 1 day in 5 is a bit outside the range, so being a little outside is common. "About 60" means it does nearly the same every day.
Some cards have a note a manager could know, such as a vacation or a change for the whole company.

For each card you answer two short questions, and sometimes a third. There are no right or wrong answers: we want your own judgment. The study takes about 30 minutes. You can take a short break at any time; your answers are saved as you go.

glossary.means: one thing the agent asks the code server to do, such as reading a file
an action that edits or adds something, such as changing a file
one folder of the company's code
a work item, such as a bug to fix
a proposed change to the code that someone reviews before it is used
the company marked that project as holding secrets or private data
this agent did not use it in its last 3 months
this agent used it on only 1 or 2 days in its last 3 months
something the agent sends to the code server, such as a file or a long comment
doing the same action on the same item again within 10 minutes
a private connection to the company from outside the office (often called a VPN); during these months the company replaced the old secure link with a new one
the person or team the agent works for
a program that runs by itself, with no person using it

text.glossary_note: Sizes are in pages of text. All times are in the owner's local time (for bots, the server's clock).

unusual.text: How unusual is this day for this agent?

check.text: Would you ask someone to check what it did today?

stood_out.text: What stood out? Pick any that apply.
stood_out.when: asked only when the answer to the first question is not "Normal for it"

pair.text: These two agents worked on the same day. There is time to check only one of them today. Which one should be checked?

sections.practice: First, two practice cards. After each one you see how we would answer it.
sections.practice_after: Real cards are often less clear than these two. "A bit unusual" and "Maybe" are fine answers when you are not sure.
sections.cards: Now the real cards. Judge each one on its own.
sections.break: You are halfway through the cards. Take a short break if you like.
sections.pairs: Last part: pairs of agents from the same day, shown line by line.
